subject: Key witness proxy ceremony and ephemeral BYO plan for private deployment
messages:
From: Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@vaultops.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@datawave.com>, support+security@datawave.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed 'key witness' proxy ceremony + ephemeral BYO flow for your Private deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for taking time to walk through DataWave's private deployment checklist last week. As we move toward the onboarding window (targeting late September), our cloud security team asked us to propose a short, auditable "key witness" ceremony for BYO keys that maps to your on‑prem HSM integration.

High-level ask: can Redwood participate in a 90-minute remote ceremony where we:
- present the ephemeral wrapping key flow (short TTL encryptions for ingress)
- validate HSM attestation artifacts and operator separation controls
- capture signed witness logs for our auditors

I've attached a proposed procedure and a lightweight diagram. Can you confirm who from Redwood should be present (engineer + compliance rep + operator) and whether your HSM vendor can provide remote attestation statements?

Attachments: key-witness-procedure-v1.pdf, ephemeral-keyflow-diagram.png

Best,
Aisha Morgan
Senior SRE, VaultOps (on behalf of DataWave security)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@vaultops.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed 'key witness' proxy ceremony + ephemeral BYO flow for your Private deployment

Aisha — thanks, this looks good.

We can run the ceremony from our Private deployment team side. Proposed Redwood attendees:
- Marcus Lin (Platform eng) — will run the HSM/KMS bridge steps
- Jonas Weber (Infra lead) — will validate network isolation and audit shipment
- Me (Security & Compliance lead) — will co‑sign witness logs and verify the attestation chain
- Kimberly Park (Ops) — will supervise operator separation and rotation ops

Couple of clarifications before we lock the slot:
1) Attestation format: does DataWave need TPM quotes, HSM vendor's signed certs, or both? We can gather PKCS#7 signed attestations and TPM quotes if needed, but we want to scope correctly.
2) Rotation window: we recommend a 24‑hour golden window for the ceremony to reduce overlap with routine rotations; confirm if that works.
3) Witness logs: we'll produce a signed, time‑stamped witness file and a short audit digest you can import into your compliance repo. If DocuSign or equivalent is required for the MOU, share the link — we have a completed template we can sign.

If that aligns, Marcus — can you prepare a short runbook and a minimal test harness that uses an ephemeral wrapping key (TTL 15m) and demonstrates unwrap-only HSM policy? I've attached a blank runbook template in the Drive link.

Neha
Neha Kapoor | Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@vaultops.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed 'key witness' proxy ceremony + ephemeral BYO flow for your Private deployment

Thanks — drafted the runbook and captured a minimal validation plan. Key points and technical checks I want on the agenda:

Runbook highlights (attached: ephemeral-keyflow-diagram.png, key-witness-procedure-v1.pdf):
- Network prep: whitelist only the management jump host IPs between DataWave's VPC egress and Redwood's on‑prem HSM gateway; mTLS required for all KMS calls.
- HSM attestation: we'll request the vendor's signed cert chain + a local TPM quote from the operator host. If vendor provides PKCS#7, we accept it.
- Ephemeral wrapping key flow: DataWave uploads a customer-wrapped key blob to Redwood staging; Redwood uses ephemeral wrapping keys (15m TTL) to encrypt ingress payloads, stores only wrapped blobs in transit. Unwrapping requires: HSM policy + operator approval token (time-limited).
- Operator separation: operator A performs provisioning, operator B performs quorum approval to enable unwrap. We will demo a split‑operator flow (2 of 3 threshold) using our operator-control plane.
- Evidence: signed witness log (SHA256 digest) + audit trail exported to Drive. We will not persist raw key material in logs.

Test matrix for the ceremony:
1) Happy path: vendor attestation accepted, wrap -> unwrap within TTL using quorum approval.
2) Expired TTL: demonstrate unwrap failure and revocation path.
3) Attestation mismatch: present a stale cert to show rejection and required remediation.
4) Failure recovery: operator-eviction and emergency zeroize path — show timeline and audit.

DocuSign: Neha, please circulate the MOU link and I'll get it signed by engineering.

Attachments: ephemeral-keyflow-diagram.png (diagram), key-witness-procedure-v1.pdf (runbook draft)

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Platform Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@datawave.com>
To: Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@vaultops.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed 'key witness' proxy ceremony + ephemeral BYO flow for your Private deployment

Neha / Marcus / team — this looks great, thanks for the thorough plan. Confirming:
- DataWave will provide HSM vendor PKCS#7 certs + a TPM quote from our admin host.
- We are happy with the 15m TTL for ephemeral wrapping keys and the 24‑hour ceremony window.
- We'll sign the MOU via DocuSign (link: DocuSign: MOU-4532-DataWave-Redwood) and book a 90‑minute slot the week of Sep 20.

Action items before the ceremony:
- Neha: share the DocuSign link and Redwood attendees' corporate DNs for the attestation chain.
- Marcus: paste the runbook link (cloud drive) with the test matrix as an executable checklist.
- Aisha: provide vendor certs and the TPM quote artifact.

Looking forward — minor ask from compliance: include the audit digest format in the runbook (simple JSON with timestamp, actor id, operation, digest).

Bryan Lee
Head of Cloud Security, DataWave Inc
